description: We are Jovidon and Nuriddin, a motivated team from Tajikistan 🇹🇯 passionate about programming, technology, and space exploration. We have interests in PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, web development, and scientific research. Our goal is to use NASA's open data to explore innovative solutions inspired by the Pamir Mountains. We welcome teammates skilled in Python, GIS, satellite data analysis, UI/UX design, and astronomy. Let's build something meaningful together!
summary: PAMIR TO MARS is an open web platform that asks: which places on Earth look like Mars, and where exactly does the resemblance stop? We compare high-altitude sites of the Pamir Mountains (Tajikistan), a region almost absent from analog research, with Gale Crater on Mars and the lunar south pole, using only open NASA data (NASA POWER, Curiosity REMS, GIBS, Mars and Moon Trek). Every value shows its source unit period and data type. A transparent Environmental Similarity Index (ESI) scores pressure, surface temperature, solar radiation and impact geology; missing data is never counted as zero, weights are adjustable, and differences are shown openly (for example, pressure at Lake Karakul is still ~80 times higher than at Gale). A 3D globe of Earth, Mars and the Moon lets anyone click any point on Earth to get its climate similarity to Mars and its closest known analog (Atacama, Ladakh, Qaidam and others). It matters because analog sites are scarce and tools that compare them honestly, with sources and limits, are rare. The code is open (MIT) and reproducible.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

PAMIR TO MARS is an open web platform that answers one question: which places on Earth resemble Mars, and where exactly does the resemblance stop? We compare high-altitude sites of the Pamir Mountains (Lake Karakul, Murghab, Ak-Baital) with Gale Crater on Mars and lunar reference sites. Our anchor idea: Lake Karakul lies inside an impact structure about 52 km across at about 3,960 m, a natural parallel to the 154 km Gale Crater explored by Curiosity.

 

NASA open data (NASA POWER climate, Curiosity REMS, GIBS, Mars Trek, Moon Trek, Earth Impact Database) is imported once into MySQL and served by a read-only API. Every value shows its source, unit, period and one of five data types: measured, satellite, modelled, calculated or interpretation. A transparent Environmental Similarity Index (ESI) scores surface pressure (log scale), surface temperature, solar radiation and impact geology: ESI = sum(w x s) / sum(w) over the parameters that have both values. Missing data is excluded, never counted as zero; weights are adjustable sliders; completeness is always shown. Example: Karakul vs Gale gives ESI about 0.66 from 3 of 4 parameters, and we show openly that pressure at Karakul is still about 80 times higher than at Gale.

 

WHAT YOU CAN DO

A 3D globe of Earth, Mars and the Moon (rotate, zoom from orbit to ~10 m imagery) with pins for the Pamir sites; "Analyze any point": click anywhere on Earth and get its climate similarity to Mars and its closest known analog among nine places (Ladakh, Qaidam, Atacama, Dry Valleys and others); a similarity heatmap of 30 NASA POWER grid cells; a crater-to-crater flight from Karakul to Gale at the same scale; best-season chart; and a data registry with formula and limitations.

 

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Analog sites are scarce and High Asia is almost absent from analog research. The platform gives scientists, teachers and students an open, reproducible way to compare places with sourced data and a formula anyone can read, and to see differences instead of hiding them. We aim to grow it into an atlas of Mars-like places on Earth: verify sites with SRTM, add Mars Climate Database and annual Curiosity values, LRO Diviner data for the Moon, and let researchers add and cite new analogs.

TOOLS

PHP and MySQL (PDO, prepared statements), JavaScript, CesiumJS (3D globe), Leaflet (fallback map), Chart.js, Tailwind CSS. Open data and imagery: NASA POWER, NASA PDS (Curiosity REMS), NASA GIBS, NASA Mars Trek (Viking, MOLA), NASA Moon Trek (LRO), Earth Impact Database, ESA Sentinel-2 by EOX. Developed and tested on Windows with OpenServer; 31 automated tests; MIT licence on GitHub; a static copy runs on GitHub Pages for any phone or computer.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

It is not another map: it turns a regional idea into a testable instrument. The honesty is the design: "pending, never zero", differences shown on screen, a 3D globe with a crater-to-crater flight, and a click-anywhere analyzer that lets anyone ask "how Mars-like is my place?".

 

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty (the Pamir is not identical to Mars or the Moon; ESI is a similarity index, not a habitat suitability score; Earth and Mars elevation datums are not subtracted; the Moon has no atmosphere, so only relief and craters are compared). Reliability (data cached in MySQL, a saved static copy if the server or NASA is offline, rate-limited NASA requests). Security (prepared statements, strict input validation, read-only API, secrets kept out of the browser and the repository, admin with login, CSRF protection and an audit log). Accessibility (phone and desktop, text badges instead of colour only). Known limits, published openly: Gale annual temperature and solar radiation are not loaded yet, some coordinates are marked "to verify" (SRTM), and the Moon is compared by relief and craters only.
